answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud. Because one person can create endless keys but cannot multiply locked tokens, Sybil accounts do not multiply influence for free; scaling them means buying or borrowing more capital and risking its loss. A river of tiny accounts may look like a pulse of support, but stake-weighted voting keeps it from carving a canyon in reputation without costly collateral.
